source_line: Source: Yahoo Finance market close, Nov. 19, 2026
caption:
Wall Street just had one of its worst days in weeks — and if you own a 401(k), you own this drop.

The Dow fell about 1,100 points Thursday (roughly 2.2%), the S&P 500 slid about 2% for its sixth straight losing day, and the Nasdaq dropped about 2.2% (Yahoo Finance, Nov. 19). The 'fear gauge,' the VIX, jumped about 16% to near 28.

Why it matters even if you never watch the market: the S&P 500 is the backbone of most retirement accounts, so a 2% down day trims the balance millions are counting on. Even Nvidia's blowout earnings this week couldn't turn the mood — the new worry is the Fed signalling rates may go up, not down.

My take: six red days is unnerving, but a 401(k) is measured in decades, not days — the headline number matters far less than the one on the day you actually retire.
